anomalies.observed: The two M5Stack bus connectors are not wired identically. On the odd (left) pin column, J1 shows the labels PWM1_C1 then PWM1_C2, while J2 shows PWM1_C1 then PWM2_C1 on the corresponding pin (pin 21). The ch.2 source net PWM2_C1 therefore sits on the odd pin 21 of J2 instead of on the even pin 20.
anomalies.expected: J1 and J2 are the top and bottom bus connectors of a stacking board and must carry the same net on every pin (spec: "identical nets on both so the board can be stacked"), with the ch.1 PWM sources on bus pins 19/21 and the ch.2 sources on bus pins 20/22.

evidence.quote: Top and bottom M5Stack bus connectors; identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through).
R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2
J1 pin 21 net label "PWM1_C2" versus J2 pin 21 net label "PWM2_C1" (root sheet, m5-pantilt.kicad_sch)

anomalies.impact: The pin-to-pin pass-through between the top and bottom bus connectors is broken for that bus pin, and the PWM2 source net is no longer on the bus pin that the M5Stack core actually drives. Depending on which connector the core mates with, the tilt (PWM2) channel can be left without a driver, and a module stacked underneath no longer sees the core's signal on that pin.

parsed.summary: The design is largely consistent with the specification, but the two M5Stack bus connectors are not net-identical as required: the same bus pin (pin 21) is labelled PWM1_C2 on J1 and PWM2_C1 on J2, so the stacking pass-through and the PWM2 source routing deviate from the intended design.
